interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado; DUAS retas numéricas de 0 a 1, uma para cada quantidade (rotuladas "Amount Lamara ate" e "Amount Orlando ate"); para cada reta há um campo onde o aluno digita em quantas partes iguais dividi-la (com confirmação) e, depois, marca o ponto da fração correspondente; abaixo, um seletor em que o aluno escolhe UMA destas alternativas: "Lamara ate more of his sandwich."; "Orlando ate more of his sandwich."; "Both ate the same amount of their sandwich."; botão Hint; botão Done. Os passos do aluno são ações NESSES componentes (dividir cada reta, marcar cada ponto, escolher a alternativa, concluir).

dicas.texto: Which number tells how many equal parts make up the whole sandwich?
Look at the denominator of Lamara's fraction and use it as the number of equal intervals.
In 2/3, the denominator is the number below the fraction bar.
Type the denominator of 2/3 into the denom1 field and confirm the division.
The numerator tells how many equal parts were eaten.
Starting at 0, count equal intervals until you reach the numerator's number of parts.
On the line divided into thirds, move two equal intervals from 0.
Click the second division point on Lamara's number line and confirm the fraction shown by that point.
Which number in Orlando's fraction tells the total number of equal parts?
Read the denominator of Orlando's fraction and use it to create equal intervals from 0 to 1.
In 2/4, the denominator is 4, not the numerator.
Type the denominator of 2/4 into the denom2 field and confirm the division.
The numerator tells how many of the equal parts were eaten.
Starting at 0, count the required number of equal intervals on Orlando's number line.
Because the numerator is 2, move two intervals from 0 on the line divided into fourths.
Click the second division point on Orlando's number line and confirm the fraction represented by that point.
Which marked point is farther to the right on the number line?
Compare the locations of 2/3 and 2/4 rather than comparing the denominator numbers alone.
Both fractions have numerator 2, so compare the size of the equal pieces shown by the two number lines.
Select the option naming the student whose marked point is farther from 0.
What can you notice when the numerator is smaller than the denominator?
Check each fraction to see whether its numerator is less than its denominator.
In both 2/3 and 2/4, the numerator 2 is smaller than the denominator.
After confirming that both fractions are less than 1 and the comparison is selected, press the Done button.

exercicio.statement:
Lamara and Orlando bought equal-sized fish sandwiches for lunch, and they are enjoying their sandwiches together. Use the number line to find out which student ate more of their sandwich.
Lamara ate 2/3 of his sandwich.
Orlando ate 2/4 of his sandwich.
Who has eaten more of their sandwich?
